lessonRef.subject: ready-for-life
lessonRef.title: Supervised application: transport and logistics over time

objective: Learners review a full month's fictional transport-and-logistics plan with a trusted adult so a second, more experienced perspective checks its feasibility before the learner relies on a plan that only looks good on paper.
scenario: The learner drafts a fictional month's plan for getting to a fictional job or set of appointments using realistic transport modes for their actual situation (which might include walking, public transit, rideshare, a ride from someone, or biking — not assuming a personal car), then reviews it with an adult who checks feasibility and suggests at least one backup option.
safetyNotes: The plan does not assume the learner has, or will have, a personal vehicle; any realistic combination of transport modes is acceptable.
No real ride-share account, real payment method, or real trip is required — the plan and its review are entirely on paper.

simulationAlternative.description: If no adult is available for a live review today, the learner self-checks the plan against a provided feasibility checklist (does every leg have a named mode, a backup for at least one leg, and a plan for bad weather or a missed connection) and notes any item the checklist flags.

materials: the fictional household plan from earlier lessons

tasks.directions: Before drafting, list every transport mode that's realistically available to you, even ones you don't usually use.

prompts.text: List every transport mode that is realistically available to you or your fictional household (walking, transit, biking, rideshare, a ride from someone, etc.), even ones you wouldn't normally choose.

tasks.directions: Draft the fictional month's transport plan, then review it with an adult for feasibility.

prompts.text: I drafted a transport plan covering the fictional month's regular trips.
I reviewed the plan with an adult, or self-checked it against the provided feasibility checklist.
The plan includes at least one backup option for at least one leg of the trip.

tasks.directions: Revise the plan based on the feedback or self-check.

prompts.text: What did the review (adult or self-check) reveal that you hadn't considered, and how did you revise the plan?
Which single leg of your plan is most likely to fail on a bad day, and does your backup for it actually work?

remediation: If the plan has no backup option anywhere (a single point of failure with no alternative), reteach by having the learner identify the one leg most exposed to disruption (weather, a missed connection, an unavailable ride) and add a specific backup for that leg before resubmitting.
extension: Have the learner redraft the plan assuming their primary transport mode becomes unavailable for one full week, and show how the fictional month's plan adapts.
